claim: Size of the combinatorial ionizable-lipid library.
locus_a: Abstract, p.1: 'A combinatorial library of 384 lipids was screened'; Results first line, p.4: 'a library of 384 ionizable lipids ... 12 headgroups, four tails, two subtails and four linkers'; Supplementary Fig. 1 caption: '12x4x2x4 = 384 unique lipids'; Fig. 1c/1h caption: '384 ionizable lipid candidates'.
locus_b: Introduction, p.2: 'a combinatorial library of more than 300 ionizable lipids was synthesized'.
what_we_emitted: 384. 03_enumerated.csv has exactly 384 rows, 12 x 4 x 4 x 2, all 384 structures distinct.
why: Three independent statements plus the block arithmetic give 384; the Introduction's 'more than 300' is a loose restatement, not a second count, and 384 satisfies it.

locus_a: Fig. 1 caption: 'o,p, Representative bioluminescence images 6 h after intrathecal injection (o) and intratracheal instillation (p)'; the panel's own heading reads 'Intratracheal instillation (0.25 mg kg-1)'.
locus_b: The same panel's y-axis label text reads 'Radiance Intrathecal injection (photons per s per cm2 per sr)' -- character-identical to panel o's axis label.
why: Two independent statements (caption and panel heading) say intratracheal and only the axis label says intrathecal; the axis label is a verbatim duplicate of the neighbouring panel's, which is the signature of a copied text box. The doses differ too (0.05 vs 0.25 mg/kg), and the panel heading carries the 0.25 figure.

claim: SAXS phase fractions must sum to 100%.
locus_a: Supplementary Table 4, row 'Fluc mRNA / 7.4 / ALC-0315': lamellae 81.5%, inverse hexagons 16.5% -- sum 98.0%.
locus_b: The other 17 rows of the same table all sum to exactly 100.0%.
what_we_emitted: nothing; SAXS phase fraction is not a delivery endpoint and is not a corpus value.
why: Recorded as a printed-statistic failure in 07_qc.json P8 (metric: max |lamellar + hexagonal - 100| = 2.0). One row in eighteen is a typo in one of the two percentages; which one cannot be told from the table.

claim: LC-lipid-5's molecular formula versus its own 1H NMR integration.
locus_b: The 1H NMR list on the same line integrates to 2+2+10+21+54+9+9 = 107 H.
what_we_emitted: nothing; no SC/LC lipid except LC-1 is mapped onto an enumerated member, so neither number is used.
why: 07_qc.json P10: nine of the ten named lipids integrate to their printed H count EXACTLY; LC-lipid-5 is the only one off, by +2 H. A 2H discrepancy is within normal integration slop for a crude listing, but it is the paper's own inconsistency and is recorded rather than averaged away.

claim: Which comparisons Fig. 1n's two significance brackets denote.
locus_a: Fig. 1 caption: 'Statistical significance was determined using a one-way ANOVA with multiple comparisons (PLC-1 vs. ALC-0315 < 1.00 x 10-15, PLC-1 vs. LP-01 < 1.00 x 10-15)'.
locus_b: The two brackets DRAWN in the panel end at x = 159.89 / 237.65 pt and x = 239.12 / 283.24 pt, i.e. ALC-0315 -> LC-1 and LC-1 -> LC-5. LP-01's group centre is 171.10 pt and no bracket reaches it.
what_we_emitted: values only; no P value is emitted.
why: 07_qc.json P3 uses the bracket endpoints as a second witness to the x-position -> lipid-name mapping, and they land on group centres to within 0.735 pt (half a marker width). The mapping is unaffected; what is inconsistent is which pair the second bracket labels.

claim: Size of the Cas9 mRNA used in Fig. 1q,r.
locus_a: Fig. 1 caption, p.2: 'transfected with Fluc (~1.7 kb), Cas9 (~4.1 kb) or ABE8.8-m (~5.7 kb) mRNAs'.
locus_b: The Fig. 1q and Fig. 1r panel labels both read 'Cas9 mRNA (Around 4.4 kb)'.
what_we_emitted: nothing; Fig. 1q,r is not extracted this pass (00_value_sources.json).
why: Recorded because if Fig. 1q,r is extracted later the cargo size goes on every one of its rows and the two loci disagree by 0.3 kb.

claim: Identity of the human embryonic kidney line.
locus_a: Results, p.4: 'human HEK293, HepG2 and BEAS2B cells'.
locus_b: Fig. 1 caption ('human (HEK293T, HepG2, BEAS2B) cells'), the Fig. 1r panel label ('HEK 293T cell'), the caption's own P-value list ('HEK293T, Cas9 editing: ...') and Methods ('HepG2, C2C12 and HEK293T cells were cultured in DMEM').
what_we_emitted: nothing; Fig. 1q,r is not extracted this pass.
why: HEK293 and HEK293T are different lines (293T carries SV40 large T). Four loci say 293T against one saying 293, so 293T is almost certainly right -- but Model_target would be set from this string, so it is recorded rather than silently resolved.

locus_a: Published title: 'Lipid nanoparticles optimized for large RNA cargo and tissue targeting enhance in vivo genome editing'.
locus_b: The curation tracker's title: 'Lipid nanoparticles optimized for large RNA cargo and tissue tropism'.
why: Same DOI (10.1038/s41587-026-03298-8) and same PMID (42806111); the tracker entry predates or paraphrases the final title. Recorded so nobody concludes these are two papers.

claim: What the asset named 'Source Data Fig. 1' contains.
locus_a: The article landing page lists 'Source Data Fig. 1' among its four supplementary assets.
locus_b: Its description on the same page is 'Sanger sequencing results', and the file (MOESM3) is six pages of chromatograms, one per cell line of Fig. 1q,r. It holds no per-lipid screening value.
what_we_emitted: nothing from it; the 384-lipid screen is recorded as NOT EXTRACTABLE in 00_value_sources.json.
why: Not a contradiction in the science, but the one that most easily wastes a curation: an asset whose NAME promises the screen reported in Fig. 1c-l and whose CONTENT is the editing panels' raw traces. A source-data sheet is not necessarily a screen.
